findings.summary: Scope: crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs changed but is not on the expected-deliverables list
findings.evidence: The diff stat lists crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs (+28/-4). The expected deliverables are docs/spec.toml, steward.rs, CHANGELOG.md and docs/enforcement.md. The file was in the planned files. It was needed because its fixtures built valid items with one job, and criterion 4 requires updating such fixtures. It holds test changes only.

findings.summary: Soundness: for proposals the rule counts any two references, such as two code paths, as two instances, so it barely tests generality
findings.evidence: steward.rs:1008 counts every distinct non-source reference for a proposal. The new test accepts a proposal resting on BRIEF.md and docs/spec.toml. In the evidence snapshot, only 4 of 185 work items have a single evidence entry, and a typical real proposal (20261110-180505-8n93) cites 9 references. So the proposal half of the rule will rarely bite, and two files about one bug pass as a 'general weakness'. A stronger alternative is to count independent instances for proposals too, such as distinct jobs, introspections or audits. The repeated-failure half, which counts distinct existing jobs, is sound. The CHANGELOG and spec say the rule is partial, and the user accepted a reading that said 'two distinct evidence references'.

findings.summary: The steward prompt does not state the two-instance rule, so items that break it are dropped after the model has spent effort on them
findings.evidence: STEWARD_PROMPT in crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs:123 says 'citing sources and evidence by reference' and says nothing about two instances. Prompt changes were out of scope, and the CHANGELOG says the prompt is unchanged. A follow-up could tell the model the rule, so it does not produce items that will be refused.

summary: The change passes: it gives OLY-5-07 a real mechanism. validate_item in steward.rs now refuses a repeated-failure item that cites fewer than two distinct existing jobs. It also refuses a proposal that cites fewer than two distinct references other than its own source. Blind spots are exempt. The refusal reason names the key and says 'one instance is not a general weakness'. The spec row names the mechanism, owner Athena, and the measure 'cargo test -p athena-core steward; status: not shown'. The new test one_instance_is_not_a_general_weakness passes with the check, and Athena's revert run shows it fails without it (exit 101). I ran the athena-core steward tests (36 passed), the CLI steward tests (12 passed), the hestia tests (81 passed), all xtask tests including the spec and enforcement-map checks, and the refusal corpus (23 passed). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full-test results passed. All six criteria are met. There are three minor findings. First, a planned CLI test file changed outside the expected deliverables. Second, the proposal half of the rule is weak, because any two file paths count as two instances, and real proposals usually cite many references (in the evidence snapshot, only 4 of 185 work items cite a single one). Third, the steward prompt does not tell the model about the new rule.
